title: introduce-token-lifecycle-sampler-and-contextual-alert-router
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add token-lifecycle sampler which creates compact per-invocation sketches and a contextual-alert-router that routes alerts based on sampled invocation fingerprints and tenant priority. Includes dashboard tiles and runbook links.
description: Motivation: long-tail token cost/latency spikes have been noisy and hard to triage because existing sampling treats tokens homogeneously. This PR introduces a lightweight token-lifecycle sampler that tags samples with phase (prefetch, generation, postprocess), prompt-shape fingerprint, and prioritized tenant metadata, and a contextual-alert-router that suppresses or escalates alerts depending on sample density and tenant priority. Changes include runtime sampler, an in-memory reservoir keyed by invocation fingerprint, alert routing policy, dashboard panels, tests and docs. Checklist: [x] implement sampler and reservoir; [x] wire sampler into invocation pipeline; [x] add contextual-alert-router with policy config; [x] add dashboard tiles and runbook links; [x] unit and integration tests; [x] e2e on staging. Related work: ENG-3421 (token sampling design), ENG-3509 (alert escalation policy). Linear tasks and design docs linked internally. Impact: reduces alert noise for low-volume tenants while preserving high-fidelity traces for high-impact invocations. Rollout: feature gated behind telemetry.token_lifecycle.enabled and staged rollout to 10% of production traffic then 100% after monitoring window. See associated dashboard: console/dashboards/token-lifecycle-sampler-overview. Implementation notes: sampler keeps up to 256 fingerprints per shard, uses reservoir sampling with age decay to prefer recent anomalies, and annotates spans with sample_reason and sample_score. Router supports config by team and SLO tier and can route high-priority signals to paging, mid-priority to e-mail, and low-priority to Slack digest. Security: no user PII is added to samples; KMS-backed signing used on sample fingerprint keys for tamper-evidence.

notes_for_oncall: If alert noise spikes after rollout, toggle telemetry.token_lifecycle.enabled=false and check metrics token_lifecycle.sample_rate and alert_router.suppressions_active. Runbook link: docs/observability/token-lifecycle-sampler.md#runbook.
postmerge_tasks: schedule follow-up ENG ticket to add cross-shard deduplication (ENG-3625)
iterate on default policy thresholds after 2 weeks of telemetry
user_visible_changes: New dashboard 'Token Lifecycle Sampler Overview' and a new toggle telemetry.token_lifecycle.enabled. Alert behavior will change for low-volume tenants (will see fewer noisy pages).
testing_and_validation: Unit tests cover reservoir eviction and sample annotation; integration tests run sampler + router with synthetic traffic profiles; staged e2e run against staging mirrored traffic for 24h. Load testing shows CPU overhead <2% at 10k invocations/s on a telemetry shard.
risk_assessment: Low-medium. Sampler is feature-gated and has conservative defaults. Risk vectors: memory usage under extreme multi-tenant churn, alert routing misclassification. Mitigations: shard-level caps, metrics for sample_queue_length, suppression_rate, and kill-switch toggle.
